saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 1ης Μαρτίου — «Όσιος Αγάπιος από τη Σκήτη της Κολιτσούς και οι μετ’ αυτού τέσσερις όσιοι»

attestations.note: The day's line couples him with «οι μετ’ αυτού τέσσερις όσιοι», the four venerable ones with him, and the page behind it names none of the four, so they are not folders here. The page puts his skete under Vatopedi, reports from Gerasimos Smyrnakis that the place took its name from his elder, the hesychast Koletios, and says the service for him was composed by St Gerasimos Mikragiannanitis and by Charalampis Bousias. It notes that St Nicodemus the Hagiorite has the pirates Saracens whom Agapius turned and baptised, while others have them Agarenes who sold him as a slave, and it gives Magnesia as the place of his slavery and twelve years as its length. «Ο χρόνος της ασκήσεως τους είναι άγνωστος» — the time of their ascesis is unknown — so the page carries no year, and the corpus's own late-eighteenth-century reading, read off doxologia, is left as it stands. The page prints no hymn and names a portable icon of him at the monastery of Karakallou, of 1943. **saint.gr keeps a second Agapius of this skete on 15 Μαρτίου**, «Όσιος Αγάπιος ο εν Σκήτη, Κολιτζοϋ» (https://www.saint.gr/03/15/index.aspx, read 1 October 2026), and the page behind that line holds no life at all: «Δεν έχουμε λεπτομέρειες για τον βίο του Αγίου». One row per church is the schema, so the day is recorded here. Whether the two lines are one man rests on the name together with the skete and on nothing else, and the settled rule is that two entries on one calendar are two commemorations — so this is a reading left open, not a second row and not a second folder.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 14.03.2026 (1. март ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Агапије.“

attestations.note: Read onto this folder because the Prologue's entry is this man's story and not another Agapius's: a novice under a spiritual father at Vatopedi — the monastery the skete of Colciu stands beside — taken by sea-robbers, held twelve years, and freed wonderfully by the Mother of God. The corpus keeps several other men of the name and none of them has any of that.

hymns.text: Ascultând de cuvintele bătrânului celui sfânt ai socotit desfătare a robiei batjocură şi vas al iubirii te-ai arătat trăgându-i pre stăpâni către Hristos. Pentru-aceea, fericite Agapie, cântându-ţi cu osârdie, strigăm: Slavă lui Hristos, Celui ce te-a slăvit, Slavă Celui ce pre tine te-a iubit, Slavă Celui ce tare mijlocitor pre tine nouă te-a dăruit.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Agapie de la Colciu

english.text: Obeying the words of the holy elder, thou didst count the mockery of slavery a delight, and wast shown to be a vessel of love, drawing thy masters to Christ. Therefore, blessed Agapius, singing to thee with zeal we cry: Glory to Christ who glorified thee, glory to him who loved thee, glory to him who gave thee to us as a strong intercessor.
